stories.title: Thermal receipt printer via Web Serial API from POS dashboard
stories.description: The built-in POS dashboard has no printing capability, requiring staff to hand-write or verbally relay orders to the kitchen. Web Serial API (Chrome 89+) allows direct browser-to-USB/serial connection to standard thermal printers (Epson TM series, Star Micronics), eliminating the need for a native app or print driver install on the kitchen tablet.
acceptanceCriteria: A 'Print Ticket' button appears on each order card in the POS dashboard
Clicking Print Ticket triggers a Web Serial connection request the first time (browser permission prompt)
The printer connection is cached in-session so subsequent prints do not re-prompt
A thermal-formatted ticket is printed with: Order ID, items x quantity, total RM, ETA, customer contact (last 4 digits masked)
If Web Serial is not supported (non-Chrome browser), the button falls back to window.print() with a print-optimised CSS layout
A 'Printer not connected' toast is shown if the serial port is unavailable
The feature is only rendered in the admin/POS route (not customer-facing)
technicalNotes: Web Serial API: navigator.serial.requestPort() — requires HTTPS and user gesture
Epson thermal printers use ESC/POS command set. Send raw bytes: ESC @  (init), ESC a 1 (center align), then text, then GS V 0 (cut)
Library: escpos-buffer (npm) simplifies ESC/POS command generation
Feature detection: if (!('serial' in navigator)) { fallback to window.print() }
Reference: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/serial
Star Micronics printers support StarPRNT protocol — check printer model before choosing command set

stories.title: Admin sold-out quick toggle per menu item
stories.description: When a dish sells out mid-service, admin currently must open the full item edit modal to update availability. A dedicated sold-out toggle (one tap) in the admin menu table and POS dashboard lets kitchen staff instantly hide a sold-out item from the customer-facing menu without navigating through the full edit flow. This is a core operational need in any busy F&B operation.
acceptanceCriteria: Each row in the admin Menu tab has a toggle switch labelled 'Available' / 'Sold Out'
Toggling sends a PATCH /api/admin/menu/[id] with { available: false } and optimistically updates the UI
Sold-out items are immediately hidden from /[locale]/menu for all customers (no cache lag — revalidateTag or revalidatePath called server-side)
Sold-out items display a greyed-out 'Sold Out' badge in the admin menu table so staff can track what's out
A 'Restore All' button in the menu tab bulk-sets all sold-out items back to available (e.g. at start of next day)
The toggle is also accessible from the POS dashboard order card as a quick inline action
Changes persist to the database (menu_items.available column)
technicalNotes: Add available BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE to menu_items if not already present
Use Next.js revalidatePath('/[locale]/menu') or revalidateTag('menu') in the API route after update
The toggle should be a shadcn/ui Switch component for accessibility
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath
Debounce rapid toggling: 300ms delay before sending PATCH to prevent double-fire on fast taps

stories.title: Allergen icon badges for common food allergens
stories.description: Beyond Halal-friendly status, customers with food allergies (nuts, shellfish, dairy, eggs, gluten) have no way to identify safe menu items from the website. Malaysian F&B businesses increasingly display allergen information following CODEX STAN 1-1985 standards. Adding per-item allergen badge icons improves food safety and signals professionalism to health-conscious diners.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin can tag menu items with one or more allergens from a predefined list: Nuts, Shellfish, Dairy, Eggs, Gluten, Soy
Allergen tags are stored as a JSONB array in the menu_items table (allergens column)
Each allergen renders as a small icon badge on the menu card with tooltip on hover / tap for the full allergen name
Icons use a consistent visual language (colour-coded): red for Nuts, orange for Shellfish, yellow for Dairy, etc.
A 'Filter by allergen-free' option appears in the menu filter to hide items containing a chosen allergen
Allergen labels are translated in all 3 locales (en/ms/zh)
Allergen information is included in the MenuItem schema.org structured data as suitableForDiet or additionalProperty
technicalNotes: ALTER TABLE menu_items ADD COLUMN allergens JSONB DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb
Predefined list: ['nuts', 'shellfish', 'dairy', 'eggs', 'gluten', 'soy'] — stored as lowercase slugs
Icon library: Lucide does not have allergen icons; use custom SVG icon set or emoji fallbacks
Reference: https://www.fda.gov/food/food-labeling-nutrition/food-allergies (labelling standards)
Malaysia CODEX reference: https://www.moh.gov.my/index.php/pages/view/44
The filter should use URL query params (?allergenFree=nuts) for shareability

stories.title: Customer pre-order cancellation within 2-minute grace period
stories.description: Customers who submit an order by mistake have no self-service way to cancel — they must contact the cafe directly. A 2-minute grace period cancellation window (industry standard for online food ordering, e.g. Grab Food) reduces waiter interruptions and improves customer trust. After 2 minutes or after admin approval, the cancel button disappears.
acceptanceCriteria: The order status page /order/[id] shows a 'Cancel Order' button for the first 120 seconds after order creation
The cancel button displays a countdown timer: 'Cancel (1:43 remaining)'
Clicking Cancel shows a confirmation prompt, then sends DELETE /api/orders/[id]/cancel
The cancellation endpoint verifies: order is in pending_approval status AND created_at is within 120 seconds of now
On successful cancellation, status is set to 'cancelled' and the customer sees a confirmation with a 'Back to Menu' CTA
The admin Orders panel shows cancelled orders in a distinct colour with a 'Cancelled by customer' label
After 120 seconds OR after admin approval, the Cancel button is hidden and the endpoint returns 403
technicalNotes: Add 'cancelled' as a valid status value to the orders table check constraint (or just the application layer)
Client-side: use a useEffect setInterval countdown; on expiry, hide the button
Server-side: check created_at + INTERVAL '120 seconds' > NOW() in the cancellation handler
No auth required for the cancellation endpoint — the order ID (nanoid) is the implicit token
Reference: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes/reference/rest (pattern for time-limited resources)
Notify admin via SSE event when a customer cancels so the bell count updates

stories.title: Admin internal notes field per order
stories.description: Admin staff need a place to record operational notes on individual orders that are invisible to customers: special prep instructions, allergy confirmations, partial substitutions agreed over the phone, or payment discrepancies. An internal-only notes field enables this without polluting the customer-facing order status page.
acceptanceCriteria: An 'Internal Notes' textarea appears in the admin order detail view (expandable, not shown by default to save space)
Notes are saved via PATCH /api/admin/orders/[id] with { adminNotes: string } to a new admin_notes TEXT column
Notes are autosaved after 1 second of typing inactivity (debounced) with a subtle 'Saved' indicator
Admin notes are NEVER returned by GET /api/orders/[id] (customer-facing endpoint) or GET /api/settings
Notes persist across page reloads and appear pre-populated when the order detail is reopened
A note icon badge appears on the order card list row to indicate 'this order has notes'
technicalNotes: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN admin_notes TEXT
Ensure GET /api/orders/[id] SELECT list does NOT include admin_notes — explicitly list columns
Use debounce(saveFn, 1000) from lodash-es or a custom hook
Reference: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-altertable.html
Character limit: 500 chars maximum (enforce on client and server)

stories.title: Admin dashboard daily sales summary widget
stories.description: The admin panel shows orders but has no aggregate view of daily performance. A simple stats bar showing today's order count, total revenue (RM), and average order value gives the owner a quick snapshot without exporting to a spreadsheet. This is the most commonly requested addition to F&B admin dashboards.
acceptanceCriteria: A stats bar at the top of the admin Orders tab shows: Orders Today (count), Revenue Today (RM), Avg Order Value (RM), Pending Approval (count)
Stats are computed from the database via GET /api/admin/orders/stats?date=YYYY-MM-DD
Stats exclude cancelled and rejected orders from revenue totals
The date defaults to today (Malaysia timezone UTC+8) but can be changed with a date picker
Stats refresh every 60 seconds automatically while the admin panel is open
Stats are shown in a horizontal card strip on desktop; stacked 2x2 grid on mobile
technicalNotes: Query: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(total), AVG(total) FROM orders WHERE DATE(created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur') = $date AND status NOT IN ('cancelled', 'rejected')
New route: GET /api/admin/orders/stats — requires verifyAdminToken()
Use Intl.NumberFormat('ms-MY', { style: 'currency', currency: 'MYR' }) for RM formatting
Reference: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/NumberFormat
Malaysia timezone: 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur' (UTC+8, no DST)

stories.title: PDPA-compliant privacy notice for customer data collection
stories.description: Malaysia's Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (PDPA) requires businesses to notify individuals when collecting personal data, state the purpose of collection, and disclose third-party sharing. The pre-order form collects contact numbers and the system forwards them to WhatsApp. A brief, plain-language privacy notice on the order submission modal satisfies this legal obligation.
acceptanceCriteria: A privacy notice paragraph appears at the bottom of the order submission modal before the Submit button
The notice states in all 3 locales: the data collected (contact number, order details), the purpose (order notification and fulfilment), and that data is not sold to third parties
A link to a full /[locale]/privacy-policy page is included in the notice
The privacy policy page exists at /[locale]/privacy-policy and contains sections: Data Collected, Purpose, Retention Period, Third Parties, Contact (cafe email), Rights under PDPA
The footer links to /privacy-policy in all locale routes
The policy states data retention period (e.g., 'Order data is retained for 90 days')
technicalNotes: PDPA 2010 (Malaysia): Section 6 requires a privacy notice before or at the time of data collection
Reference: https://www.pdp.gov.my/jpdpv2/assets/2019/09/Personal_Data_Protection_Act_2010.pdf
The privacy policy page can be a static MDX file under content/ or a hardcoded RSC page
No cookie consent banner required unless using tracking cookies — the pre-order form doesn't use cookies
The notice text should be concise (2-3 sentences) with a 'Learn more' link — do not show the full policy inline

stories.title: Full Restaurant and MenuItem schema.org structured data on home and menu pages
stories.description: The site currently lacks Restaurant-level structured data on the home page and per-item MenuItem structured data on the menu page. Complete schema.org markup enables Google's restaurant rich results (showing hours, price range, cuisine in search), improves local SEO authority for 'Thai food Skudai' searches, and prepares the site for voice search (Google Assistant queries menu data directly from structured markup).
acceptanceCriteria: The home page RSC includes a Restaurant JSON-LD with: name, description, url, telephone, address (PostalAddress), geo (GeoCoordinates), openingHoursSpecification, servesCuisine, priceRange, image, hasMap
The menu page includes a Menu JSON-LD containing hasMenuSection (one per display category) each with hasMenuItem entries
Each MenuItem includes: name (in locale language), description, offers (Offer with price and priceCurrency 'MYR'), suitableForDiet where applicable
Structured data passes Google Rich Results Test without errors
JSON-LD is rendered server-side as a <script type='application/ld+json'> tag in RSC — not injected client-side
openingHoursSpecification uses ISO 8601 day-of-week format (Mo, Tu, We, Th, Fr, Sa, Su)
technicalNotes: Restaurant schema: https://schema.org/Restaurant — extends FoodEstablishment extends LocalBusiness
MenuItem schema: https://schema.org/MenuItem — note: 'nutrition' property exists but optional
GeoCoordinates: get lat/lng from Google Maps for Taman Impian Emas, Skudai
priceRange: use '$' to '$$$$' convention — for this cafe use '$$' (mid-range)
Reference: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/local-business
Cafe facts (address, hours, phone) must come from src/lib/constants.ts — do not hardcode in JSON-LD components

stories.title: Security response headers via Next.js middleware
stories.description: The site currently sets no security headers, making it vulnerable to clickjacking (no X-Frame-Options), MIME sniffing (no X-Content-Type-Options), and information leakage (no Referrer-Policy). OWASP recommends these headers as baseline hardening for any public-facing web app. Next.js middleware or next.config.ts headers can apply them globally with minimal code.
acceptanceCriteria: The following headers are set on all responses: X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()
A Content-Security-Policy header is set that allows: self, the Neon/Vercel domains, Google Fonts, and the WhatsApp/Groq API origins. Does NOT use 'unsafe-inline' for scripts.
Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header is set with max-age=31536000 on production (not localhost)
Headers are verified via https://securityheaders.com/ — minimum grade B
The X-Powered-By: Next.js header is removed from responses
The image domain whitelist in next.config.ts is reviewed and tightened (no wildcard * hostnames)
technicalNotes: Implement in next.config.ts under the headers() async function (applies to all routes)
Remove X-Powered-By: add poweredByHeader: false to next.config.ts
CSP nonce approach needed if inline scripts are used — otherwise use hash-based CSP
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/headers
Reference: https://owasp.org/www-project-secure-headers/
Test locally: curl -I http://localhost:3031/en and inspect response headers

stories.title: Offline connectivity banner for customers and staff
stories.description: In a restaurant environment with spotty WiFi, customers may lose internet connectivity while browsing the menu or submitting an order. Without feedback, users assume the app is broken. A non-intrusive offline banner (using the Navigator.onLine API and 'offline'/'online' events) clearly communicates connectivity status and prevents confusion.
acceptanceCriteria: A yellow banner appears at the top of the page when the device goes offline: 'You're offline. Some features may be unavailable.' (in all 3 locales)
The banner disappears automatically when connectivity is restored (online event fires)
The banner is dismissible via an X button
When offline, the order submission button is disabled with tooltip 'Internet required to place orders'
When offline, the menu data is still visible if it was cached by the service worker
The banner uses prefers-reduced-motion to disable its slide-in animation if the user has reduced motion enabled
technicalNotes: Listen for: window.addEventListener('offline', handler) and window.addEventListener('online', handler)
Initial state: navigator.onLine — note this can be unreliable; treat as a hint, not ground truth
Implement as a Client Component registered once in [locale]/layout.tsx
Reference: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/onLine
For accurate offline detection, use a periodic fetch to a lightweight ping endpoint (e.g. /api/ping returning 204) every 30 seconds

stories.title: API rate limiting on customer-facing order submission endpoint
stories.description: POST /api/orders has no rate limiting, making it vulnerable to automated spam submissions that would fill the admin dashboard with fake orders and overflow the Neon database. The AI chat endpoint already has per-IP rate limiting (src/lib/chat/rate-limit.ts) — this same pattern must be applied to the order submission and payment upload endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/orders is rate-limited to a maximum of 3 requests per IP per 10-minute window
POST /api/orders/[id]/payment is rate-limited to 5 requests per IP per 10-minute window
Requests exceeding the limit receive HTTP 429 with JSON: { error: 'rate_limit_exceeded', retryAfter: seconds }
The Retry-After header is set on 429 responses
The rate limiter uses an in-process Map (same pattern as src/lib/chat/rate-limit.ts) — no Redis dependency required for this traffic level
The IP is extracted from x-forwarded-for header (Vercel proxies all requests) with fallback to request.ip
technicalNotes: Reuse and extend src/lib/chat/rate-limit.ts — extract a generic createRateLimiter(maxRequests, windowMs) factory
Vercel provides the client IP via the x-forwarded-for header: request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for')?.split(',')[0]
In-process Map resets on cold starts — acceptable for the traffic volume of a small cafe
Reference: https://vercel.com/docs/security/vercel-firewall (for platform-level rate limiting if needed)
Reference: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Retry-After

stories.title: Custom Next.js 404 and app-level error pages
stories.description: The site currently uses Next.js default error pages, which are unstyled and off-brand. Custom 404 and error pages maintain the Makan Moments brand experience, offer helpful navigation back to key pages, and prevent users from feeling stranded. F&B sites lose customers who hit a 404 without a clear 'Browse Menu' fallback CTA.
acceptanceCriteria: A custom /src/app/[locale]/not-found.tsx renders a branded 404 page with: a food-themed illustration or emoji, the message 'Page not found' in all 3 locales, and CTA buttons to /menu and /
A custom /src/app/[locale]/error.tsx renders a branded error boundary page with a 'Try Again' button that calls reset()
A custom /src/app/[locale]/global-error.tsx handles root layout errors
The 404 page preserves the site header and footer
The 404 page has correct HTTP 404 status code (not 200) — verified via curl -I
Both pages are localized (use getTranslations or hardcoded translations for the 3 locales)
technicalNotes: Next.js App Router: not-found.tsx is the file convention for 404 pages (works with notFound() thrown in any RSC)
error.tsx must be a Client Component ('use client') and receives { error, reset } props
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error
The [locale] segment means each locale gets its own not-found.tsx — place one under src/app/[locale]/not-found.tsx

stories.title: Rich PWA manifest with screenshots for Android enhanced install UI
stories.description: The current manifest.json triggers only the minimal Android install banner. Adding a screenshots array to the manifest activates Chrome's 'Enhanced Install Dialog', which shows app screenshots and a description before the user installs — significantly increasing install conversion. This complements the existing customer install prompt story (which handles the JS deferral logic) but focuses on the manifest content.
acceptanceCriteria: public/manifest.json includes a screenshots array with at least 2 screenshots: one showing the menu page and one showing the order tracking page
Each screenshot entry includes: src (path), sizes (e.g. '1080x1920'), type ('image/png'), form_factor ('narrow'), and a descriptive label
The manifest includes a description field (max 200 chars) summarising the app purpose in English
The manifest includes a categories array: ['food', 'shopping']
Screenshot images are real app screenshots at 1080x1920 resolution (portrait, mobile)
The enhanced install dialog is verified working on Android Chrome by inspecting DevTools > Application > Manifest
technicalNotes: screenshots[].form_factor: 'narrow' for mobile, 'wide' for desktop — use 'narrow' as primary
Chrome requires at least 1 screenshot to trigger the rich install UI on Android
Capture screenshots at 1080x1920 using Chrome DevTools device emulation (iPhone 14 Pro resolution)
Reference: https://web.dev/articles/add-manifest#screenshots
The manifest.json is already referenced in src/app/layout.tsx or next.config.ts — just update the file

stories.title: Admin printable order ticket with kitchen-optimised layout
stories.description: Staff sometimes need a physical copy of an order to hand to the kitchen chef, especially during rush periods when verbal communication is unreliable. A print-optimised order ticket using CSS @media print removes navigation and renders a clean, large-font kitchen chit. This requires no hardware integration — just window.print() with a purpose-built print stylesheet.
acceptanceCriteria: A 'Print Ticket' button appears in the admin order detail view
Clicking Print opens the browser print dialog with a pre-rendered kitchen ticket layout
The print layout shows: order ID (large, bold), arrival ETA, items with quantities (font-size ≥ 14pt), total, and any customer notes
Navigation header, footer, sidebar, and action buttons are hidden in print via CSS (@media print { display: none })
The ticket fits on a single A5 page in portrait orientation
The admin notes field is NOT included in the printed ticket (internal only)
technicalNotes: Use @media print CSS in a <style> tag or globals.css to show only the ticket component
Add a print-specific class (e.g. .kitchen-ticket) to the ticket component; everything else gets @media print { display: none }
Call window.print() from a button onClick handler
Reference: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Guide/Printing
For thermal label printers (80mm roll), set @page { size: 80mm auto; margin: 5mm } in the print stylesheet

stories.title: Progressive image loading with LQIP blur-up for menu item photos
stories.description: Menu item photos are the primary visual content of the site, but they load as a blank space until fully downloaded on slow connections. Low-Quality Image Placeholders (LQIP) — tiny blurred base64 thumbnails shown while the full image loads — dramatically improve perceived load time and prevent layout shift. Next.js Image supports this natively via the placeholder='blur' prop.
acceptanceCriteria: All menu card images use Next.js <Image> with placeholder='blur' and a blurDataURL
The blurDataURL is a 4x4 pixel base64 JPEG placeholder generated at build time or on first load
The blur effect transitions smoothly to the sharp image when loading completes (CSS transition: filter 0.3s ease)
LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) metric for the menu page does not regress — LCP hero image uses priority={true} and does NOT use blur placeholder (priority images load immediately)
The implementation works for both statically hosted images (public/images/menu/) and externally hosted images (if admin uploads to a CDN)
CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) score for the menu page is 0 — images have explicit width and height attributes
technicalNotes: Next.js Image blur placeholder: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#placeholder
Generate blurDataURL with: npx plaiceholder generate --input public/images/menu/*.jpg (or use the plaiceholder npm package)
Store blurDataURL per menu item in the database or as a computed field in the menu data
Alternative: use a CSS background-color placeholder matching the dominant colour (simpler, no blur)
Reference: https://web.dev/articles/lcp (LCP optimisation)
Do NOT apply blur to the hero image — it must load immediately (priority={true})

stories.title: iOS Safari PWA meta tags for standalone mode and status bar styling
stories.description: iOS Safari requires Apple-specific meta tags for a proper standalone PWA experience. Without these, the PWA added to the iPhone home screen displays the browser address bar (breaking the app illusion), uses incorrect status bar colours, and shows a generic Safari icon instead of the app icon. These are distinct from the W3C manifest and must be added separately.
acceptanceCriteria: The root layout includes: <meta name='apple-mobile-web-app-capable' content='yes'> to enable standalone mode on iOS
The root layout includes: <meta name='apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style' content='default'> (or 'black-translucent' to extend into status bar area)
The root layout includes: <meta name='apple-mobile-web-app-title' content='Makan Moments'> for the home screen label
Apple touch icons are provided at public/apple-touch-icon.png (180x180px) and linked via <link rel='apple-touch-icon'>
When the PWA is launched from the iOS home screen, no browser address bar is visible
The splash screen background colour matches the site's warm cream theme (#faf7f2 or equivalent)
technicalNotes: Add meta tags to src/app/layout.tsx or via Next.js metadata API: metadata.appleWebApp
Next.js supports apple-touch-icon via metadata: appleWebApp: { capable: true, title: '...', statusBarStyle: 'default' }
Reference: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/AppleApplications/Reference/SafariWebContent/ConfiguringWebApplications/ConfiguringWebApplications.html
Apple touch icon must be exactly 180x180px PNG with no transparency for iOS home screen
Splash screens for different iOS device sizes can be added via apple-touch-startup-image meta tags (optional but recommended)

stories.title: Re-order shortcut from customer order history
stories.description: Repeat customers who visit the cafe regularly have the same orders (e.g., their usual nasi lemak and teh tarik). A 'Re-order' button on the order history page that pre-populates the tray with items from a past order reduces friction for loyal customers and increases order conversion speed. This builds on the pending order history page story.
acceptanceCriteria: Each past order card on /[locale]/orders has a 'Re-order' button
Clicking Re-order populates the TrayContext with all items from that past order (respecting current quantities from localStorage order history)
If a past order item no longer exists in the current menu (by item ID), it is silently skipped and a toast shows: 'Some items are no longer available and were removed'
After Re-order, the user is navigated to /[locale]/menu with the tray widget open
The tray shows the pre-populated items and a summary of total RM
Re-ordering does not immediately submit an order — it just fills the tray for the customer to review
technicalNotes: Compare past order item IDs against the current menu data fetched client-side
Use TrayContext.addItem() for each valid past order item
Trigger tray open state via a context method or URL param: /en/menu?trayOpen=1
Reference: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/localStorage
Past order items schema: [{id, nameEn, price, quantity}] — already stored in mm_order_history

stories.title: Order status change outbound webhook for third-party integrations
stories.description: Business owners using tools like n8n, Zapier, or Make (formerly Integromat) need to automate downstream workflows triggered by order status changes (e.g., send a WhatsApp group message when an order is ready, log to Google Sheets, trigger a loyalty reward). An outbound webhook on status change enables this without custom backend code.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin can configure a webhook URL in site settings (webhook_url field, optional)

When any order status changes (via PATCH /api/admin/orders/[id]), the system fires a POST to the configured webhook URL with a JSON payload: { event: 'order.status_changed', orderId, newStatus, oldStatus, timestamp, total, contactNumber }
The webhook is sent asynchronously and does NOT block the admin response
If the webhook URL returns a non-2xx status, the failure is logged but the order update still succeeds
The webhook payload includes an HMAC-SHA256 signature header (X-Webhook-Signature) using a configurable webhook secret, so the receiver can verify authenticity
The admin Settings tab has a 'Test Webhook' button that sends a sample payload to the configured URL
technicalNotes: Use fetch() with a 5-second timeout in a non-blocking fire-and-forget pattern: void sendWebhook(payload)
HMAC signature: crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(JSON.stringify(payload)).digest('hex')
Store webhook_url and webhook_secret in data/site-settings.json (never expose secret via public GET /api/settings)
Reference: https://webhooks.fyi/ (webhook best practices)
Reference: https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads (signature pattern)
n8n has a built-in Webhook trigger node that can receive this payload directly
